newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee sees possible restart this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee sees possible restart this weekend.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear power station may restart this weekend following an unexpected trip off line Wednesday during routine testing of its reactor protective system, the plant operator said Friday.
"It could be as early as this weekend," said Maureen Brown, spokeswoman for Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co when asked about the latest startup schedule.
Today's Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) daily status report showed a Friday restart for Maine Yankee.
Late Thursday, the operator issued a statement indicating Maine Yankee would likely return on line next week.
A preliminary review showed the shutdown of Maine Yankee was caused by a dip in power supply in circuit board used only during the monthly testing of the system.
"They replaced that circuit board...They've completed a number of tests, and they have a followup review," said Brown.

Maine Yankee Atomic Power operates the 910 megawatt facility in Wiscasset, Maine, and is owned by a consortium of New England utilities including Central Maine Power Co 38 percent; New England Electric System 20 percent; and Northeast Utilities 20 percent.
